root_cause.text: The vulnerability exists because `devm_kzalloc` in `btusb_probe` tied the lifetime of the shared `btusb` data structure to the INTF interface, causing premature memory deallocation when that interface disconnects while other interfaces (ISOC, DIAG) still reference the data.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description states that `devm_kzalloc` ties the lifetime of all the btusb data to the binding of a driver to one interface, INTF, and that `btusb_disconnect()` calling `usb_driver_release_interface` will have devm free the data that is also being used by the other interfaces of the driver that may not be released yet.

relevance_review.reason: No code changes or core intent were provided for Group 0, so it cannot address the vulnerability regarding devm_kzalloc lifetime management.

The vulnerability root cause involves premature memory deallocation due to incorrect resource lifetime binding (tying `btusb` to INTF interface). Group 2 addresses a memory leak during initialization error handling (`hci_alloc_dev_priv` failure). These are distinct issues: one concerns runtime lifecycle management across interfaces, while the other concerns cleanup during driver probe failure.

vuln_statements.explanation: This devm_kzalloc call in btusb_probe ties the lifetime of the shared btusb data structure to the INTF interface device. When the INTF interface disconnects, devm_kzalloc automatically frees the memory, causing premature deallocation while other interfaces (ISOC, DIAG) still hold references to the now-freed data structure. This is the root cause of the use-after-free vulnerability.
